hero.name: Vesper Hearthkeeper
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

event.title: The arms that first held you
event.body: Elowen Hearth decides what kind of shelter to make around this new life. A handwritten note survives in a schoolbook. Your household knows the value of patient work. Two parents: Elowen Hearth (parent), Mara Hearth (parent), Tamsin Hearth (sibling), Bram Hearth (sibling). A secure roof; household support 65/100. Not currently enrolled; free schools open at six, and independent reading remains a choice. Cold ash warmed your blanket although the hearth was dark. Your family will remember the sign; its meaning must be discovered through childhood.

choices.description: Elowen Hearth builds Vitality, practical curiosity, and village connections.

journal.text: Vesper Hearthkeeper is born in Mossbell. Household circumstances shape opportunities; no class has been chosen. Your guardians make the first decisions.

journal.title: The arms that first held you
journal.text: Elowen Hearth chose to ask and investigate. Your intellect grew through care and experience.

journal.title: A teacher accused without a hearing
journal.text: Inspect the lamp and reconstruct the accident. Gain scholarship and arcana. Evidence keeps community classes open.

journal.title: The seedling under the broken cart
journal.text: Find a way to lift the wheel without breaking the roots. Gain scholarship and survival. A careful repair becomes part of your education.

journal.title: The Cinderbound omen · age 4
journal.text: At four, a cold fireplace shows unfamiliar hands tending its coals. Only the person beside you sees you reach toward them.

journal.title: The light beneath the hill
journal.text: You chose to ask and investigate. You developed scholarship and arcana.

journal.title: The keeper’s missing fox
journal.text: Study the tracks and prepare a gentle remedy. Gain survival and arcana. Find one useful herb bundle.

journal.title: A door into named lessons
journal.text: Community and shrine schools now offer free enrollment. Independent reading remains available if you do not enroll.

hero.name: Vesper Hearthkeeper
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

event.title: A useful place in the world
event.body: The guild board has room for people who intend to stay as well as adventurers passing through. None of these professions changes your combat path. Each earns a living and practices a different skill.

choices.label: Assist the village healer
choices.description: Become a Healer. Work earns 24 gold and practices devotion.

choices.label: Learn a merchant’s trade
choices.description: Become a Merchant. Work earns 28 gold and practices persuasion.

choices.label: Copy and teach academy lessons
choices.description: Become a Scholar. Work earns 23 gold and practices scholarship; certification increases wages.

choices.label: Apprentice to an herbalist
choices.description: Become a Herbalist. Work earns 23 gold, practices survival, and gathers remedy components.

choices.label: Join the local watch
choices.description: Become a Soldier. Work earns 26 gold and practices weapons; serving a settlement is a livelihood.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Vesper Hearthkeeper is born in Mossbell. Household circumstances shape opportunities; no class has been chosen. Your guardians make the first decisions.

hero.name: Vesper Hearthkeeper
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Vesper Hearthkeeper is born in Mossbell. Household circumstances shape opportunities; no class has been chosen. Your guardians make the first decisions.

journal.title: The arms that first held you
journal.text: Elowen Hearth chose to ask and investigate. Your intellect grew through care and experience.

journal.title: A first winter
journal.text: Elowen Hearth chose to ask and investigate. Your intellect grew through care and experience.

journal.title: The words you keep
journal.text: Elowen Hearth chose to ask and investigate. Your intellect grew through care and experience.

journal.title: A teacher accused without a hearing
journal.text: Inspect the lamp and reconstruct the accident. Gain scholarship and arcana. Evidence keeps community classes open.

journal.title: The seedling under the broken cart
journal.text: Find a way to lift the wheel without breaking the roots. Gain scholarship and survival. A careful repair becomes part of your education.

journal.title: The Cinderbound omen · age 4
journal.text: At four, a cold fireplace shows unfamiliar hands tending its coals. Only the person beside you sees you reach toward them.

journal.title: The light beneath the hill
journal.text: You chose to ask and investigate. You developed scholarship and arcana.

journal.title: The keeper’s missing fox
journal.text: Study the tracks and prepare a gentle remedy. Gain survival and arcana. Find one useful herb bundle.

journal.text: Community and shrine schools now offer free enrollment. Independent reading remains available if you do not enroll.

journal.title: The missing silver charm
journal.text: You chose to ask and investigate. You developed scholarship and arcana.

journal.title: The tune that did not belong to the festival
journal.text: Compare the song with the school’s oldest book. Gain scholarship and arcana. Keep a remembered discrepancy for later research.

journal.text: Inspect the lamp and reconstruct the accident. Gain scholarship and arcana. Evidence keeps community classes open.

journal.title: A teacher asks what you want

journal.title: The Cinderbound omen · age 10
journal.text: At ten, you notice that the old cistern stones are warm beneath the rain. The warmth moves toward the city, against the water’s flow.

journal.title: The tune that did not belong to the festival
journal.text: Compare the song with the school’s oldest book. Gain scholarship and arcana. Keep a remembered discrepancy for later research.

journal.title: An education with open doors
journal.text: You chose to ask and investigate. You developed survival and persuasion.

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

hero.name: Vesper Hearthkeeper
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

event.title: Room beside the hearth
event.body: The guardian explains that a child needs time, steady support, and a person who will stay. Wren Moss is willing to welcome a child together. You have spent thirty gold preparing the home and consulting the guardian.

choices.label: Offer a child a permanent home
choices.description: Adopt a child through the village guardian. Support costs 45 gold per year.

choices.label: Welcome a child together
choices.description: Welcome a child into a shared household with your partner’s freely given agreement. Support costs 45 gold per year.

choices.label: Keep the preparations and wait
choices.description: Add no child yet. The consultation and home supplies have already been paid for.

hero.name: Vesper Hearthkeeper
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Morrow Reach

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Goldmere Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fernbridge Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Wrenwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Wrenwood Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Hearth Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Silver Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Silver Teeth Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Sable Marsh
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Sable Marsh Alder Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Moonward Spire
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Moonward Spire Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Copper Caravan Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Brassward Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Bastion of Bells Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Ancestor’s Rest Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is permitted; in Fernbridge, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Wrenwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

memories: You invited me to travel as a healer, without asking me to forget my family.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families
memories: You invited me onto the road while respecting my search for my sibling.

hero.name: Lark
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Rowan Vale

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Mossbell Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Hearth Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Candlewick
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Candlewick Wren Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Millbrook
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Millbrook Lantern Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Millbrook Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin Rowan Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Frostglass Range
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Frostglass Range Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Mourning Mire
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Mourning Mire Hearth Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ivory Strand
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Ivory Strand Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Astral Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Astral Stair Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Ember Encampment
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Ember Encampment Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Kingsroad Gate
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Kingsroad Gate Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Ivory Citadel
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Alder Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Hearth Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Candlewick, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is forbidden; in Millbrook, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Scholars debate in public courtyards, while the rural shrines keep older traditions alive.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Candlewick is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Lantern Thicket can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Rowan Bell
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Physician Sable
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: The Grey Finch
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.
