world.name: The Rowan Vale

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Mossbell Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Hearth Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Candlewick
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Candlewick Wren Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Millbrook
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Millbrook Lantern Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Millbrook Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin Rowan Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Frostglass Range
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Frostglass Range Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Mourning Mire
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Mourning Mire Hearth Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ivory Strand
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Ivory Strand Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Astral Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Astral Stair Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Ember Encampment
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Ember Encampment Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Kingsroad Gate
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Kingsroad Gate Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Ivory Citadel
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Alder Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Hearth Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Candlewick, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is forbidden; in Millbrook, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Scholars debate in public courtyards, while the rural shrines keep older traditions alive.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Candlewick is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Lantern Thicket can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Rowan Bell
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Physician Sable
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: The Grey Finch
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

event.title: Your rival’s name beside yours
event.body: Your former rival completes a useful community survey with you. A patron offers to publish it under your name alone. The choice affects an actual person who may later be willing to help your research. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Last year, your choice to ask and investigate was remembered. Your household has little money, but people can offer time and teaching. An unsettled shelter household: Corin Reed (shelter guardian), Anwen Reed (sibling), Neris Reed (sibling). Birth parent 1 · identity unrecorded: missing; Birth parent 2 · identity unrecorded: unknown. These people are not offered as living contacts. No secure roof yet; household support 0/100. Not currently enrolled; free schools open at six, and independent reading remains a choice.

choices.label: Insist that the survey carry both names
choices.description: Gain 12 rival bond and academy trust. They remember fair credit.

choices.label: Release the survey for anyone to use
choices.description: Gain scholarship and village trust. Both names remain in the record.

choices.label: Accept the patron’s terms
choices.description: Earn 25 gold but lose 15 rival bond. The rival remembers the missing credit.

world.name: The Rowan Vale

locations.name: Mossbell
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Mossbell Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Mossbell Hearth Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Candlewick
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Candlewick Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Candlewick Wren Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Millbrook
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Millbrook Lantern Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Millbrook Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Alder Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: Saint Orin’s Ruin Rowan Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Frostglass Range
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Frostglass Range Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Mourning Mire
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Mourning Mire Hearth Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Ivory Strand
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Ivory Strand Alder Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Astral Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Astral Stair Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Ember Encampment
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Ember Encampment Hearth Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Kingsroad Gate
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Kingsroad Gate Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Ivory Citadel
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Ivory Citadel Alder Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Hearth Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Candlewick, necromancy is regulated; in Mossbell, it is forbidden; in Millbrook, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Scholars debate in public courtyards, while the rural shrines keep older traditions alive.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Candlewick is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Lantern Thicket can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Rowan Bell
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Physician Sable
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: The Grey Finch
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.

event.title: Your rival’s name beside yours
event.body: Your former rival completes a useful community survey with you. A patron offers to publish it under your name alone. The choice affects an actual person who may later be willing to help your research. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Last year, your choice to ask and investigate was remembered. Your household has little money, but people can offer time and teaching. An unsettled shelter household: Corin Reed (shelter guardian), Anwen Reed (sibling), Neris Reed (sibling). Birth parent 1 · identity unrecorded: missing; Birth parent 2 · identity unrecorded: unknown. These people are not offered as living contacts. No secure roof yet; household support 0/100. Not currently enrolled; free schools open at six, and independent reading remains a choice.

choices.description: Earn 25 gold but lose 15 rival bond. The rival remembers the missing credit.
